title: AI Product Design & Copilot Ergonomics | Senior Product Design Specialist Durga Prasad
desc: Intuitive copilot surfaces, generative UI patterns, and human-in-the-loop validation tools.
lead: Bridging the gap between probabilistic AI models and deterministic human expectations.
body: Most AI products fail because they treat an LLM as a novelty chat box slapped onto an old interface. I design AI-native interfaces that surface confidence intervals, provide inline editable suggestions, respect context windows, and give users total control over automated actions.
bottlenecks: Designing for non-deterministic AI latency and conversational streaming states
Communicating model confidence without misleading users on edge-case hallucinations
Creating granular human review controls (Accept, Edit, Reject, Rollback)
Moving beyond generic chat interfaces into inline contextual workspace suggestions
principles: AI should propose, but the human must always dispose.
Never hide what data was used to reach an AI conclusion; citation is trust.
Latency states should feel purposeful: progressive token rendering and skeleton previews.

faqs.q: Why is a chat interface often the wrong choice for enterprise AI?
faqs.a: Chat forces users to imagine prompt queries from scratch and review unstructured paragraphs. Contextual cards, inline diffs, and structured recommendation widgets are significantly faster for enterprise workflows.

faqs.q: How do you handle AI hallucinations in the UI?
faqs.a: By designing confidence thresholds that prompt the human when ambiguity is high, displaying explicit citations, and allowing 1-click manual inline overrides.

title: Dashboard UX & Data Visualization | Senior Product Design Specialist Durga Prasad
desc: High-density data tables, responsive charting, and multi-parameter filtering systems.
lead: Transforming dense enterprise data dumps into clear visual decision engines.
body: Dashboards shouldn't be vanity metric graveyards. They exist to trigger informed decisions. I architect enterprise dashboards with visual hierarchy, scannable summary cards, customizable data tables, and intuitive drill-down paths that allow executives and operators to spot anomalies in seconds.

stats.label: Rows rendered with zero cognitive drag

bottlenecks: Preventing cognitive paralysis caused by displaying 40 charts simultaneously
Designing high-density data tables with bulk actions, sorting, pin columns, and cell editing
Structuring progressive query filters that adapt to complex boolean parameters
Ensuring charts are fully legible across color-blind palettes and diverse screen resolutions
principles: Summary first, zoom and filter, then details-on-demand (Shneiderman's Mantra).
Every visualization must answer an actionable question: 'So what should I do now?'
Tables are software: pagination, sticky headers, and keyboard row traversal are mandatory.

faqs.q: How do you decide what belongs on the main dashboard view?
faqs.a: We conduct operator interviews to identify the top 3 decisions made daily. Only metrics directly feeding those 3 decisions make the primary viewport; everything else is accessible via drill-downs.

faqs.q: What makes an enterprise table usable?
faqs.a: Configurable columns, persistent filters, sticky header/row IDs, batch actions, and high cell contrast without decorative padding bloat.

title: Design Systems & Token Architecture | Senior Product Design Specialist Durga Prasad
desc: Scalable design token manifests, headless components, and governance workflows.
lead: Bridging the chasm between Figma files and production code with pixel precision.
body: A design system is not a UI kit; it is a shared language and technical contract between designers and engineers. I build robust design token architectures (colors, spacing, typography, radii, shadows) mapped directly to Tailwind, React, and CSS variables, eliminating design drift forever.
bottlenecks: Preventing design token fragmentation across legacy and modern tech stacks
Enforcing strict component variant matrices (sizes, states, accessibility rings)
Standardizing accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1 AA) at the atomic token layer
Creating automated handoff documentation that developers actually use and respect
principles: Every design decision traces back to a token: Primitive → Semantic → Component.
If a component variant cannot be built cleanly in code, it should not exist in Figma.
A living style guide must be zero-build and self-contained for complete transparency.

proof.raw: EyeOnTask Unified PlatformWeb & Mobile component parity ↗

faqs.q: Do you provide code or just Figma files?
faqs.a: Both. I define the design token manifest directly in TypeScript/CSS and provide clean, accessible React component templates matching Tailwind configurations.

faqs.q: When should a startup invest in a design system?
faqs.a: As soon as you have more than 2 engineers building interfaces simultaneously. Without tokens, inconsistency compounds into technical debt exponentially.

body: In fintech, visual ambiguity equals financial anxiety. A delayed confirmation toast, a poorly phrased button, or an unexpected modal will cause users to immediately suspect fraud or failure. I design fintech flows with military-grade clarity, instant state feedback, and psychological reassurance.
bottlenecks: Compressing complex multi-step KYC/AML verification without hurting conversion
Designing instant optical feedback during high-stakes payment gateway transitions

Communicating regulatory compliance without overwhelming consumer comprehension
principles: Every microsecond of latency must be communicated with clear progress states.
Never present a surprise fee at the final transaction confirmation step.
Visual reassurance (lock icons, verification badges, clear summaries) reduces cart abandonment.

faqs.q: How does design impact fintech compliance?
faqs.a: Careful UX ensures legal disclosures are genuinely readable rather than ignored legalese, reducing regulatory risk and chargeback disputes.

faqs.q: How do you measure success in B2B SaaS UX?
faqs.a: We track Product Qualified Lead (PQL) activation rate, Time-to-Value (TTV), feature adoption depth, ticket volume submitted to support for workflow confusion, and net revenue retention.

faqs.q: How do you handle technical debt while redesigning a SaaS app?
faqs.a: We decouple UX redesign into modular workflow sprints. Rather than a risky complete rewrite, we overhaul the most painful funnel leaks (such as onboarding and main dashboard views) incrementally.
